title: ADF / NDB
src: R.K. Bali — Air Navigation, Part III Ch 2 (key read from the printed answer grid, PDF p. 245)

qs.q: Direction property error is known as?
What is used to resolve 180° ambiguity?
o: Align radio compass to True North

qs.q: An aircraft is flying on a heading of 315°. Which of the following (magnetic) signal bearings will cause the maximum quadrantal error?
qs.ex: Signal from 360° on heading 315° arrives at relative bearing 045°, a quadrantal (inter-cardinal) bearing: maximum error. 225° and 135° arrive at 270° and 180° relative: no error.

qs.q: Variations of signal in NDB receivers due skywaves indicates the presence of:
The BFO selector on an ADF receiver is used to:
o: hear the IDENT of some NDB stations radiating a continuous wave signal

qs.q: Which one of the following disturbances is most likely to cause the greatest inaccuracy in ADF bearings?
Factors liable to affect most NDB/ADF system performance and reliability include:
o: static interference- night effect- absence of failure warning system
height error- station interference- mountain effect

qs.q: There are two NDBs, one 20NM inland, and the other 50NM inland from the coast. Assuming that the error caused by coastal refraction is the same for both propagations, the extent of the error in a position line plotted by an aircraft that is over water will be:
o: greater from the beacon that is 20NM inland
the same from both beacons when the aircraft is on a relative bearing Of 180° and 360°
greater from the beacon that is 50NM inland

qs.q: What is the wavelength of an NDB transmitting on 373 kHz?
An aircraft is "homing" to a radio beacon whilst maintaining a relative bearing of zero. If the magnetic heading decreases, the aircraft is experiencing:
qs.ex: With RB 000 the nose follows the beacon; the heading falls (turning left) because the wind is pushing you right: right (starboard) drift.

qs.q: Errors caused by the effect of coastal refraction on bearings at lower altitudes are maximum when the NDB is:
o: inland and the bearing crosses the coast at an acute angle
inland and the bearing crosses the coast at right angles
near the coast and the bearing crosses the coast at right angles

qs.q: Quadrantal errors associated with aircraft Automatic Direction Finding (ADF) equipment are caused by:
o: signal bending by the aircraft metallic surfaces
signal bending caused by electrical interference from aircraft wiring

qs.q: "Night Effect" which causes loss of signal and fading, resulting in bearing errors from transmissions, is due to:
o: interference from other transmissions and is maximum at dusk when east of the NDB
static activity increasing at night particularly in the lower frequency band
skywave distortion of the null position and is maximum at dawn and dusk

qs.q: Which of the following is likely to have the greatest effect on ADF accuracy?
o: Frequency drift at the ground station
Interference from other NDBs, particularly at night

qs.q: An aircraft is maintaining track outbound from an NDB with a constant relative bearing of 184° .To return to the NDB the relative bearing to maintain is:
qs.ex: Outbound with RB 184 means 4° starboard drift. Coming back on the reciprocal, the same wind gives 4° port drift, so the nose points 4° right of the station: RB 356.

qs.q: Which statement about the NDB transmitter is correct?
o: It is operating in the HF/VHF band
It is very simple, being required to transmit only a carrier wave and identification
In India, most NDBs operate in the frequency band 455 - 1750 kHz

qs.q: The purpose of the BFO switch on the ADF receiver is to:
o: improve the strength of the received signal

qs.q: When using NDBs night effect is most likely to be greatest at:
With regard to the following types of NDB which statements is correct?
o: Locators have 200 W power, 50 nm range and are NON A2A
Locators have 5000 W power, 50 nm range and are NON A1A
Locators have 15 W power, 10-25 nm range and are NON A2A

qs.q: The D layer of the ionosphere affects the accuracy of NDB bearings:
qs.ex: Key as printed in the book.

qs.q: An ADF uses a sense aerial to:
Which of the following equipments does not have a system to warn the pilot that it is inoperative:
The BFO:
o: is used to make the ident from an A1A NDB audible
is used to determine the signal strength of an NDB
creates the audio ident for an NDB

qs.q: An NDB signal crossing from land to sea will … speed and bend … the normal.
Long range NDBs normally employ:
When using a NON A2A NDB the BFO should be:
o: off for tuning and on for identification
off for tuning and off for identification
on for tuning and off for identification

qs.q: What is the approved frequency band assigned to aeronautical ADFs?
The promulgated range for an NDB is applicable:
o: throughout 24 hours, but is most prone to error around dusk and dawn

qs.q: An aero plane is flying parallel to a coast. Which of the following NDBs will give the greatest coastal refraction LOP error?
A radio beacon has an operational range of 10 NM. By what factor should the transmitter power be increased in order to achieve an operational range of 20 NM?
qs.ex: Range ∝ √power: double the range needs four times the power.
